title: APO Cod with Silky Cider-Leek Gravy
description: Bagless cod cooks through in full steam and is served on a smooth gravy of slowly softened leek and sweet apple cider.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe, bottom drip pan and middle wire rack

ingredients.name: skinless boneless cod loin
ingredients.note: Fully thawed and pin bones removed; portion horizontally to a uniform 3/4 inch.

ingredients.name: white leek
ingredients.note: Thinly slice, rinse between the layers and drain.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water without a vegetable seasoning blend.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 140°F with sous vide mode on, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 139°F.

steps.title: Set the cod in the pan
steps.text: Lay {cod} unbagged in the shallow pan on the middle rack. Insert the probe from the side into the thickest center. Begin cooking immediately and set a separate 25-minute reminder for the first temperature check; respond sooner if the probe signals.

steps.title: Soften the leek
steps.text: While the cod steams, cover {leek}, {butter} and a spoonful of {broth} in the HexClad over low heat for 10–12 minutes until completely soft. Stir twice and add a splash more broth if needed.

steps.title: Blend the gravy base
steps.text: Add the remaining {broth}, {cider} and {parsley} and simmer for 3 minutes. Purée in a deep heatproof jug, pass through a fine sieve to remove any fibers and return the gravy to the skillet.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Steam the fish
steps.text: Cook until the probe reaches 139°F, generally 30–65 minutes from refrigerated. Start checking at 25 minutes.

steps.title: Check for doneness
steps.text: At 139°F, check the thickest center of each portion for flesh that is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. If either cue is missing, continue in the 140°F full-steam oven and recheck every 3 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Plate over gravy
steps.text: Spoon half the gravy into two shallow bowls. Lift the cooked cod onto it and ladle the remaining gravy over the fish.

notes: Make ahead: Soften and blend the leeks a day ahead and chill. Add the slurry when ready to serve. For the initial fish cook, verify both opacity and easy flaking at the stated probe target. Option A uses sweet cider. For gentler Option B, replace it with more broth. For dairy-free gravy replace the butter with avocado oil. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Delicate cod flakes can turn firm or break up after freezing; the separate gravy can be frozen for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: Place one portion and its sauce in a shallow covered dish. Install the APO bottom drip pan and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Insert the probe in the coldest center and set it to 165°F. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If previously frozen, thaw in the refrigerator overnight and use the same covered reheating method. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 158 kcal, 23.7 g protein, 8.1 g total carbohydrate, 2.9 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 87 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.

steps.title: Prepare the portions
steps.text: Divide {cod} into even portions. Leave fish fillets whole.

steps.title: Start the poach
steps.text: Warm enough water to half cover the portions in a snug Dutch oven to 175–185°F. Slide them in, cover and hold below a simmer. Start checking after 4 minutes.

steps.title: Soften the leek
steps.text: While the cod steams, cover {leek}, {butter} and a spoonful of {broth} in the HexClad over low heat for 10–12 minutes until completely soft. Stir twice and add a splash more broth if needed.

steps.title: Blend the gravy base
steps.text: Add the remaining {broth}, {cider} and {parsley} and simmer for 3 minutes. Purée in a deep heatproof jug, pass through a fine sieve to remove any fibers and return the gravy to the skillet.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the centers
steps.text: Check each center every 2 minutes and lift out as soon as it reaches 145°F.

steps.title: Plate over gravy
steps.text: Spoon half the gravy into two shallow bowls. Lift the cooked cod onto it and ladle the remaining gravy over the fish.
